روي في هذا الباب عن صخر بن وداعة الغامدي، وابن عمر، وأبي هريرة، وعلي، وابن مسعود، وعبد الله بن سلام، وأنس، وابن عباس، وعائشة، ونبيط بن شريط، وأبي بكرة، وجابر، وكعب بن مالك، والنواس بن سمعان، وعمران بن حصين، وأبي ذر، وبريدة، وواثلة، والعرس بن عميرة، وأبي رافع.

وفي كلها مقال، ولكن مجموعها يدل على أن له أصلًا.

حديث صخر بن وداعة الغامدي، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «اللهم بارك لأمتي في بكورها».

قال: فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا بعث سرية بعثها أول النهار. وكان صخر رجلًا تاجرًا، وكان لا يبعث غلمانه إلا من أول النهار، فكثر ماله حتى كان لا يدري أين يضع ماله.

رواه أحمد (١٥٤٣٨)، وأبو داود (٢٦٠٦)، والترمذي (١٢١٢)، وابن ماجه (٢٢٣٦)، وابن حبان (٤٧٥٥)، والبيهقي (٩/ ١٥١).

قال الترمذي: «حديث حسن».

وقال عبد الحق الإشبيلي: «حديث أبي داود حسن».

وقال أبو حاتم في «العلل» (٢/ ٢٦٨): «لا أعلم في اللهم بارك لأمتي في بكورها حديثًا صحيحًا».

وروي أيضًا عن ابن عمر، وأبي هريرة، وعلي بن أبي طالب، وعبد الله بن مسعود، وعبد الله بن سلام، وأنس، وابن عباس، وعائشة، ونبيط بن شريط، وأبي بكرة، وجابر، وكعب بن مالك، والنواس بن سمعان، وعمران بن حصين، وأبي ذر، وبريدة، وواثلة، والعرس بن عميرة، وأبي رافع.

قال ابن الجوزي في «العلل المتناهية» (١/ ٣١٤-٣٢٧): «هذه الأحاديث كلها لا تثبت».

وقال ابن القطان في «الوهم والإيهام» (٣/ ٤٨٨): «وليس هو عندي بصحيح».

وقال أبو حاتم: «لا أعلم فيه حديثًا صحيحًا».

قلت: وهو كما قال، ولكن تشهد كثرة شواهده، واختلاف مخارجه بأن له أصلًا، وإن لم يثبت أحد بعينه.

فالحق أنه ليس فيه صحيح أو حسن، ولكن مجموعه يفيد بأن له أصلًا.

chapters.intro_en_source:
Reports concerning this chapter have been narrated from Ṣakhr ibn Wadāʿah al-Ghāmidī, Ibn ʿUmar, Abū Hurayrah, ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, Anas, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿĀʾishah, Nubayṭ ibn Sharīṭ, Abū Bakrah, Jābir, Kaʿb ibn Mālik, al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān, ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, Abū Dharr, Buraydah, Wāthilah, al-ʿIrs ibn ʿUmayrah, and Abū Rāfiʿ.

There is criticism concerning all of them, but collectively they indicate that the report has a basis.

Ṣakhr ibn Wadāʿah al-Ghāmidī narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “O Allah, bless my Ummah in its early mornings.”

Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent an expedition, he would send it at the beginning of the day. Ṣakhr was a merchant and would only send his servants out at the beginning of the day, so his wealth increased until he did not know where to place it.

Narrated by Aḥmad (15438), Abū Dāwūd (2606), al-Tirmidhī (1212), Ibn Mājah (2236), Ibn Ḥibbān (4755), and al-Bayhaqī (9/151).

Al-Tirmidhī said: “A ḥasan hadith.”

ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq al-Ishbīlī said: “The hadith of Abū Dāwūd is ḥasan.”

Abū Ḥātim said in al-ʿIlal (2/268): “I do not know any authentic hadith concerning: ‘O Allah, bless my Ummah in its early mornings.’”

Reports were also narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, Abū Hurayrah, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, Anas, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿĀʾishah, Nubayṭ ibn Sharīṭ, Abū Bakrah, Jābir, Kaʿb ibn Mālik, al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān, ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, Abū Dharr, Buraydah, Wāthilah, al-ʿIrs ibn ʿUmayrah, and Abū Rāfiʿ.

Ibn al-Jawzī said in al-ʿIlal al-Mutanāhiyah (1/314–327): “All of these hadiths are unestablished.”

Ibn al-Qaṭṭān said in al-Wahm wa-al-Īhām (3/488): “In my view, it is not authentic.”

Abū Ḥātim said: “I do not know any authentic hadith concerning it.”

The author said: It is as he said. However, the large number of supporting routes and their differing chains indicate that it has a basis, even though no individual route is established by itself.

The correct conclusion is that there is no individually authentic or ḥasan report concerning it, but the reports collectively indicate that it has a basis.

Allah Most High said: “Woe to those who give less in measure, those who, when they take a measure from people, take in full, but when they give by measure or by weight to them, they cause loss.” [Surat al-Mutaffifin, 1–3]

And He said: “So give full measure and weight, and do not deprive people of their things.” [Surat al-A‘raf, 85]

And He said: “Give full measure when you measure, and weigh with a straight balance.” [Surat al-Isra’, 35]

And He said: “Do not reduce the measure and the weight.” [Surat Hud, 84]

ومعنى الحديث باختصار أن إخراج الزكاة من الذهب والفضة ينظر إلى ميزان أهل مكة الذي عُدل في عهد عبد الملك بن مروان لما أراد ضرب الدنانير والدراهم، فكان النصاب الذي تجب فيه الزكاة مائتي درهم، وعلى هذا يقاس جميع الدراهم في البلدان المختلفة، وإن كانت أوزانها تختلف من بلد إلى بلد.

وأما ما يتعلق بوجوب الكفارات، وإخراج صدقة الفطر، وتقدير النفقات، وما في معناه، فينظر إلى مكيال أهل المدينة، وهو ما يسمى بالصاع. وصاع أهل المدينة يختلف عن صاع أهل العراق، فصاع أهل المدينة خمسة أرطال وثلث بالعراقي، وصاع أهل العراق ثمانية أرطال.

chapters.intro_en_source:
The meaning of this hadith, briefly, is that the zakah threshold for gold and silver is judged according to the weight standard of the people of Makkah, which was formalized in the time of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan when coinage was standardized. Thus, the nisab on silver was two hundred dirhams, and other dirhams in different lands are compared against that standard even if their local weights differ.

As for matters like expiations, the charity of breaking the fast, maintenance amounts, and similar rulings, these are judged according to the measuring standard of the people of Madinah, which is the sa‘. قلت: وإسناده ضعيف.

It is narrated from Anas ibn Mālik that a man from the Anṣār came to the Prophet ﷺ asking him for assistance. He said: “Do you have anything in your house?”

He replied: “Yes, a cloth, part of which we wear and part of which we spread out, and a drinking vessel from which we drink water.”

He said: “Bring them to me.”

He brought them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took them in his hand and said: “Who will buy these two?”

A man said: “I will take them for one dirham.”

He said: “Who will offer more than one dirham?” two or three times.

Another man said: “I will take them for two dirhams.”

He gave the two items to him, took the two dirhams, and gave them to the Anṣārī. He said: “Buy food with one of them and take it to your family, and with the other buy an axe and bring it to me.”

He brought it to him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fitted a handle into it with his own hand. Then he said: “Go, gather firewood and sell it, and do not let me see you for fifteen days.”

The man went away gathering firewood and selling it. He later returned having earned ten dirhams. With some of it he bought clothing and with some he bought food.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “This is better for you than begging coming as a mark upon your face on the Day of Resurrection. Begging is not appropriate except for three: one suffering crushing poverty, one burdened by an overwhelming debt, or one responsible for painful blood-money.”

Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1641), al-Tirmidhī (1218), al-Nasāʾī (1412), Ibn Mājah (2198), and Aḥmad (11968, 12134).

Al-Tirmidhī graded it ḥasan.

The author said: Its chain is weak.

Al-Tirmidhī said: “The practice according to some of the scholars is based upon this. They saw no harm in auction sales involving spoils of war and inheritances.”

روي عن الشعبي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من وجد دابة قد عجز عنها أهلها أن يعلفوها، فسيبوها، فأخذها، فأحياها، فهي له».

رواه أبو داود (٣٥٢٤، ٣٥٢٥).

وفي رواية: «من ترك دابة بمهلك، فأحياها رجل فهي لمن أحياها».

ورواه سعيد بن منصور عن الشعبي قال: من قامت عليه دابته، فتركها، فهي لمن أحياها. قيل: عمن هذا يا أبا عمرو؟ قال: إن شئت عددت لك كذا وكذا من أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

قال البيهقي (٦/ ١٩٨): «هذا حديث مختلف في رفعه، وهو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم منقطع».

وقال ابن التركماني: «قد قدمناه في باب فضل المحدث أن مثل هذا ليس بمنقطع، بل هو موصول، وإن الصحابة كلهم عدول».

قلت: وهو كما قاله ابن التركماني، وإن كان أكثر أهل العلم مثل الخطابي والبغوي وغيرهما ذهبوا إلى أنه منقطع.

وقال بظاهر الحديث أحمد بن حنبل وإسحاق.

وأما أكثر الفقهاء فقالوا: إن ملكها لم يزل عن صاحبها بالعجز عنها، وسبيلها سبيل اللقطة، فإذا جاء ربها وجب على واجدها رد ذلك عليه.

وقوله: «حسيرًا» هو الدابة العاجزة عن المشي.

It is narrated from al-Shaʿbī that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever finds an animal whose owners have become unable to feed it and therefore abandon it, then takes it and restores it to life, it belongs to him.”

Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3524, 3525).

In another wording: “Whoever abandons an animal in a place of destruction, and another man revives it, it belongs to the one who revived it.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr also narrated from al-Shaʿbī that he said: “If a person’s animal becomes unable to continue and he abandons it, then it belongs to whoever revives it.” He was asked: “From whom is this, O Abū ʿAmr?” He replied: “If you wish, I could enumerate for you such-and-such a number of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ.”

Al-Bayhaqī said (6/198): “There is disagreement concerning whether this hadith is raised to the Prophet ﷺ, and as a report from the Prophet ﷺ it is disconnected.”

Ibn al-Turkumānī said: “We previously explained in the chapter concerning the virtue of the hadith scholar that a report such as this is not disconnected; rather, it is connected, and all the Companions are upright.”

The author said: It is as Ibn al-Turkumānī said, although most of the scholars, such as al-Khaṭṭābī, al-Baghawī, and others, held that it is disconnected.

Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and Isḥāq adopted the apparent meaning of the hadith.

Most jurists, however, said that the owner’s ownership does not cease merely because he became unable to care for the animal. Its ruling is like that of lost property; if its owner later appears, the finder must return it to him.

The word “ḥasīr” means an animal that has become incapable of walking.

It is narrated from al-Najrānī, who said:
I asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar: “May I make a salam transaction for palm fruit before it appears?”
He said: “No.”
I asked: “Why?”
He said: “A man made a salam transaction concerning a palm grove during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before the fruit appeared, but the palms produced nothing that year. The buyer said: ‘It remains mine until it produces fruit.’ The seller said: ‘I only sold you the fruit of this year.’
They took their dispute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said to the seller: ‘Did he receive anything from your palm trees?’
He replied: ‘No.’
He said: ‘Then on what basis do you consider his wealth lawful for you? Return to him what you took from him, and do not make salam transactions concerning palm fruit until its soundness becomes apparent.’”
Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3467), Ibn Mājah (2284), and Aḥmad (5067).
Al-Najrānī is unknown; his identity is not known.

Allah the Exalted said: “They said: We have lost the king’s measuring cup, and whoever brings it shall have a camel-load, and I am a guarantor for it.” [Yusuf: 72]

The words guarantor, surety, and sponsor all carry one meaning. “Zaim” is the term used by the people of Madinah, “hamil” by the people of Mudar, and “kafil” by the people of Iraq. The meaning is that whoever takes responsibility for another person’s debt becomes liable for it. This is guarantee.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
روي عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أيما رجل باع سلعة، فأدرك سلعته بعينها عند رجل قد أفلس، ولم يكن قبض من ثمنها شيئًا فهي له، وإن كان قبض من ثمنها شيئًا فهو أسوة الغرماء».
وقال دعلج: «فإن كان قضاه من ثمنها شيئًا فما بقي فهو أسوة الغرماء».
وهذا الحديث روي مسندًا ومرسلًا.
رواه الدارقطني (٣/ ٢٩)، وأبو داود (٣٥٢٢).
قال الدارقطني: «إسماعيل بن عياش مضطرب الحديث، ولا يثبت هذا الحديث عن الزهري مسندًا، وإنما هو مرسل».
ورواه مالك في «الموطأ» في البيوع (٨٧)، وأبو داود (٣٥٢٠)، وعبد الرزاق (٨/ ٢٦٤)، والبيهقي (٦/ ٤٦-٤٧) مرسلًا بلفظ: «أيما رجل باع متاعًا فأفلس الذي ابتاعه منه، ولم يقض الذي باعه من ثمنه شيئًا، فوجده بعينه فهو أحق به، وإن مات الذي ابتاعه فصاحب المتاع فيه أسوة الغرماء».
قال أبو داود: «حديث مالك أصح».
وقال في «المراسيل» (١٦٢): «روي مسندًا، وليس بالقوي، وروي مسندًا قصة الموت، وهو لا يصح مسندًا، وقصة الإفلاس مشهور صحيح مسند».
والخلاصة أن الحديث لا يصح موصولًا من طريق الزهري، وإنما المحفوظ فيه الإرسال.
وأما حديث أبي هريرة بلفظ: «من أدرك ماله بعينه عند رجل أو إنسان قد أفلس فهو أحق به من غيره» فهو مخرج في الصحيحين.
وقال الخطابي: «والحديث إن صح وثبت عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فليس إلا التسليم له، وكل حديث أصل بذاته ومعتبر بحكمه في نفسه».

It is narrated from Abū Hurayrah that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Any man who sells a commodity and then finds that very commodity with a man who has become bankrupt, while he has not received any of its price, then it belongs to him. But if he has received part of its price, then he is on equal footing with the other creditors.”
Daʿlaj said: “If the buyer has paid him part of its price, then regarding what remains he is on equal footing with the other creditors.”
This report has been transmitted both as connected and as mursal.
It was narrated by al-Dāraquṭnī (3/29) and Abū Dāwūd (3522).
Al-Dāraquṭnī said: “Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh is inconsistent in hadith, and this report is not established from al-Zuhrī as a connected report; rather, it is mursal.”
Mālik narrated it in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ, Book of Sales (87), and it was also narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3520), ʿAbd al-Razzāq (8/264), and al-Bayhaqī (6/46–47) as a mursal report with the wording:
“Any man who sells goods and the buyer becomes bankrupt without paying the seller any of the price, and the seller finds the goods themselves, then he has more right to them. But if the buyer dies, the owner of the goods is on equal footing with the other creditors.”
Abū Dāwūd said: “Mālik’s report is more authentic.”
He also said in al-Marāsīl (162): “It has been narrated as connected, but it is not strong. The report concerning death has also been narrated as connected, but it is not authentic as connected. As for the case of bankruptcy, it is well known and authentically transmitted as connected.”
The conclusion is that the report is not authentic as a connected narration through al-Zuhrī; what is preserved from him is the mursal form.
As for the hadith of Abū Hurayrah with the wording, “Whoever finds his property itself with a man who has become bankrupt has more right to it than anyone else,” it is recorded in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
Al-Khaṭṭābī said: “If the hadith is authentic and established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then nothing remains except submission to it. Every hadith is an independent foundational proof and is considered according to its own ruling.”

قال اللّٰه تعالى: ( وَلَا تُؤْتُوا السُّفَهَاءَ أَمْوَالَكُمُ الَّتِي جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ قِيَامًا ) [سورة النساء: ٥].

وقال تعالى: ( فَإِن كَانَ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ الْحَقُّ سَفِيهًا أَوْ ضَعِيفًا ) الآية [سورة البقرة: ٢٨٢].

فأثبت الولاية على السفيه، كما أثبتها على الضعيف.

ومعنى السفيه راجع إلى الكبير البالغ، ومعنى الضعيف راجع إلى الصغير.

وقال سبحانه وتعالى: ( وَابْتَلُوا الْيَتَامَى حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغُوا النِّكَاحَ فَإِنْ آنَسْتُم مِّنْهُمْ رُشْدًا فَادْفَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَالَهُمْ ) [سورة النساء: ٦]. فشرط في دفع المال إليهم شيئين: الاحتلام والرشد.

والحكم إذا كان وجوبه معلقا بشيئين لم يجب إلا بورودهما معا.

قاله الخطابي في معالمه (٤/١٥٢-١٥٣).

وهذا الحجر على عائشة لم يكن في محله؛ لأنها لم تكن سفيهة؛ فإن تصرفها كان صحيحاً، ولذا لم ترض بحجر ابن الزبير، بل شددت عليه بأن لا تكلمه أبداً.

Allah the Exalted said: “Do not give the foolish your wealth which Allah has made a means of support for you.” [al-Nisa: 5]

And He said: “If the one upon whom the obligation is due is foolish or weak…” [al-Baqarah: 282]

So He established guardianship over the foolish person just as He established it over the weak one.

The meaning of “foolish” here refers to the adult of unsound financial judgment, while the meaning of “weak” refers to the minor.

And He, Glorified and Exalted, said: “Test the orphans until they reach marriageable age; then if you perceive in them sound judgment, hand over to them their wealth.” [al-Nisa: 6] Thus He made two conditions for handing wealth over to them: puberty and sound judgment.

A ruling whose obligation is tied to two conditions does not become due unless both are present together.

This was stated by al-Khattabi in Ma‘alim al-Sunan (4/152–153).

This proposed restriction against Aishah was not appropriate, because she was not foolish in judgment. Her financial conduct was sound, and that is why she did not accept Ibn al-Zubayr’s attempt to restrict her, but instead became firm in refusing to speak to him.

And He, Glorified and Exalted, said: “Test the orphans until they reach marriageable age; then if you perceive in them sound judgment, hand over to them their wealth.” [al-Nisa: 6] Thus He made two conditions for handing wealth over to them: puberty and sound judgment.

A ruling whose obligation is tied to two conditions does not become due unless both are present together.

This was stated by al-Khattabi in Ma‘alim al-Sunan (4/152–153).

This proposed restriction against Aishah was not appropriate, because she was not foolish in judgment. Her financial conduct was sound, and that is why she did not accept Ibn al-Zubayr’s attempt to restrict her, but instead became firm in refusing to speak to him.

روي عن السائب بن أبي السائب قال: أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فجعلوا يثنون علي ويذكروني، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أنا أعلمكم به». قلت: صدقت، بأبي أنت وأمي، كنت شريكي، فنعم الشريك، كنت لا تداري ولا تماري.
رواه أبو داود (٤٨٣٦)، وابن ماجه (٢٢٨٧)، وأحمد (١٥٥٠٢).
وإسناده ضعيف لاضطراب وقع فيه.
وروى الإمام أحمد (١٥٥٠٠) عن السائب بن عبد الله قال: جيء بي إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم فتح مكة، فجعلوا يثنون عليه، فقال لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا تعلموني به، قد كان صاحبي في الجاهلية». قال: نعم يا رسول الله، فنعم الصاحب كنت. فقال: «يا سائب، انظر أخلاقك التي كنت تصنعها في الجاهلية فاجعلها في الإسلام، أقر الضيف، وأكرم اليتيم، وأحسن إلى جارك».
قال ابن عبد البر: «وهذا اضطراب لا يثبت به شيء، ولا تقوم به حجة».
وكذلك لا يصح ما روي عن أبي هريرة مرفوعًا: «إن الله عز وجل يقول: أنا ثالث الشريكين ما لم يخن أحدهما صاحبه، فإذا خانه خرجت من بينهما».
رواه أبو داود (٣٣٨٣)، والدارقطني (٣/ ٣٥)، والحاكم (٢/ ٥٢)، والبيهقي (٦/ ٦٧٧).
قال الحاكم: «صحيح الإسناد».
والصواب أنه ضعيف.
وكذلك لا يصح ما روي عن ابن عباس قال: كان العباس بن عبد المطلب إذا دفع مالًا مضاربة اشترط على صاحبه أن لا يسلك به بحرًا، ولا ينزل به واديًا، ولا يشتري به ذا كبد رطبة، فإن فعله فهو ضامن. فرفع شرطه إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأجازه.
رواه الدارقطني (٣/ ٧٨)، وقال: «فيه أبو الجارود ضعيف».

It is narrated from al-Sāʾib ibn Abī al-Sāʾib that he said:
I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and the people began praising me and mentioning my qualities. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I know him better than you do.”
I said: “You have spoken the truth, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you. You were my business partner, and what an excellent partner you were. You neither flattered nor argued.”
Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4836), Ibn Mājah (2287), and Aḥmad (15502).
Its chain is weak because of inconsistency in its transmission.
Imām Aḥmad (15500) also narrated from al-Sāʾib ibn ʿAbd Allāh that he said:
“I was brought to the Prophet ﷺ on the day of the Conquest of Makkah. They began praising me, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: ‘You do not need to inform me about him; he was my companion during the Jāhiliyyah.’”
He said: “Yes, O Messenger of Allah, and what an excellent companion you were.”
He said: “O Sāʾib, look at the good manners you practiced during the Jāhiliyyah and continue them in Islam: honor the guest, honor the orphan, and treat your neighbor well.”
Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: “This is inconsistent transmission by which nothing can be established and no proof can be based upon it.”
Likewise, the report narrated from Abū Hurayrah as a marfūʿ report is not authentic:
“Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘I am the third of two partners so long as neither of them betrays the other. When one betrays the other, I depart from between them.’”
Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3383), al-Dāraquṭnī (3/35), al-Ḥākim (2/52), and al-Bayhaqī (6/677).
Al-Ḥākim said: “Its chain is authentic.”
The correct judgment is that it is weak.
Likewise, the report from Ibn ʿAbbās that al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib would stipulate conditions when giving money for muḍārabah, and that the Prophet ﷺ approved his conditions, is not authentic.
Al-Dāraquṭnī narrated it (3/78) and said: “Abū al-Jārūd is weak.”

Allah the Exalted said: “O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of usury, if you are truly believers. But if you do not, then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger. And if you repent, then you may have your principal sums; you do not wrong, nor are you wronged. And if someone is in hardship, then let there be postponement until ease. But if you remit it as charity, that is better for you, if only you knew. And fear a Day on which you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be paid in full for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.” [al-Baqarah: 278–281]

And He said: “Those who consume usury will not stand except as one stands who has been struck by Satan into madness…” [al-Baqarah: 275–276]

In language, usury means increase. In sacred law, it means an unlawful increase in wealth, whether through excess in exchange or through delay in repayment.

فأتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في بيت حفصة، فقلت: يا رسول الله، رويدك أسألك: إني أبيع الإبل بالبقيع، فأبيع بالدنانير وآخذ الدراهم، وأبيع بالدراهم وآخذ الدنانير، آخذ هذه من هذه وأعطي هذه من هذه.
فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا بأس أن تأخذها بسعر يومها ما لم تفترقا وبينكما شيء».

Ibn ʿUmar narrated:
“I used to sell camels at al-Baqīʿ. I would sell for dinars and receive dirhams, and sell for dirhams and receive dinars, taking these in place of those and giving these in place of those.
I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in the house of Ḥafṣah and said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, allow me to ask you. I sell camels at al-Baqīʿ. I sell for dinars and receive dirhams, and sell for dirhams and receive dinars, taking these in place of those and giving these in place of those.’
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ‘There is no harm in taking them according to the exchange rate of that day, so long as you do not separate while anything remains outstanding between you.’”
Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3354), al-Tirmidhī (1242), al-Nasāʾī (4583), Ibn Mājah (2262), al-Ḥākim (2/44), al-Bayhaqī (5/284), and Aḥmad (4883).
Al-Tirmidhī said: “We do not know this hadith except through the narration of Simāk ibn Ḥarb from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿUmar. Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind narrated this hadith from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿUmar as mawqūf.”
Al-Ḥākim said: “Authentic according to the conditions of Muslim.”
The correct judgment is that the hadith is weak, and what is preserved is that it is mawqūf upon Ibn ʿUmar.
Al-Bayhaqī said: “Simāk ibn Ḥarb alone raises this hadith from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr among the transmitters from Ibn ʿUmar.”
Al-Tirmidhī said: “The practice according to some of the scholars is that there is no harm in settling gold with silver and silver with gold. This is the view of Aḥmad and Isḥāq. Some of the scholars among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ and others disliked it.”

Allah the Exalted said: “Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, the strangled animal, the beaten animal, the fallen animal, the gored animal, and that which has been eaten by a beast — except what you are able to slaughter properly — and that which is sacrificed on stone altars, and that you seek decision by divining arrows. That is grave disobedience. Today those who disbelieve have despaired of your religion, so do not fear them, but fear Me. Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and chosen submission to Allah as your religion. But whoever is forced by severe hunger, without inclining to sin, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.”

[Surat al-Ma’idah: 3]

آلاف درهم، وقال: فإن رضي عمر فالبيع له، وإن لم يرض عمر فأربعمئة لصفوان.

It is narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Farrukh that Nafi‘ ibn Abd al-Harith bought a house for use as a prison from Safwan ibn Umayyah for four thousand dirhams, and he said: If Umar approves, then the sale is binding for him, and if Umar does not approve, then four hundred belong to Safwan.

Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah (23662) and al-Bayhaqi (4/34), and its chain is authentic.

Al-Bukhari mentioned it in a suspended form after hadith (2422) and titled the chapter: “Chapter on tying and detention in the sanctuary.”

This Nafi‘ was Umar’s governor over Makkah, so he stipulated the option for Umar. Imam Ahmad adopted this and held the permissibility of earnest-money sales.

As for the hadiths reported concerning the prohibition of earnest money, none of them is established.

وقال الإمام أحمد في عهدة الثلاث في الرقيق: لا يثبت في العهدة حديث. ومعنى الخبر عند من ذكره: إن ظهر العيب في الأيام الأولى رُدَّ بغير بينة، وبعدها يحتاج المشتري إلى إقامة البينة على أن العيب كان موجودًا عند الشراء.

It is reported from ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no warranty after four [days].” It was narrated by Ibn Majah (2245), Ahmad (17292), and al-Bayhaqi (5/323). Al-Hasan al-Basri did not hear from ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir, so the scholars judged the report to be mursal and weak. Its chain is also inconsistent, as it was also narrated from al-Hasan through Samurah ibn Jundub.

Imam Ahmad said concerning the three-day warranty for slaves: no hadith concerning the warranty is established. According to those who discussed the report, its meaning is that if a defect appears during the first days, the slave may be returned without additional proof; after that period, the buyer must establish that the defect existed at the time of purchase.

روي عن ابن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى عن بيع الكالئ بالكالئ.
رواه الدارقطني (٣/ ٧١)، والحاكم (٢/ ٥٧)، والبغوي في «شرح السنة» (٨/ ١١٣)، والبزار في «كشف الأستار» (١٢٨٠).
وفي رواية البزار: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الشغار، وعن بيع المجر، وعن بيع الغرر، وعن بيع كالئ بكالئ، وعن بيع آجل بعاجل.
قال: «والمجر: ما في الأرحام، والغرر: أن تبيع ما ليس عندك، وكالئ بكالئ: دين بدين، والآجل بالعاجل: أن يكون لك على رجل ألف درهم، فيقول الرجل: أعجل خمسمائة، ودع البقية».
قال الدارقطني: «قال اللغويون: هو النسيئة بالنسيئة».
وقال الحاكم: «هذا حديث صحيح على شرط مسلم».
والصواب أنه ضعيف.
وقال أحمد بن حنبل: «ليس في هذا حديث يصح، لكن إجماع الناس على أنه لا يجوز بيع دين بدين».
وقال الشافعي: «أهل الحديث يوهنون هذا الحديث».
قال أبو عبيد: «الكالئ بالكالئ هو النسيئة بالنسيئة».
والفقهاء ضربوا له أمثلة كثيرة في بيع النسيئة بالنسيئة.

The report is narrated from Ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet ﷺ prohibited the sale of “al-kāliʾ for al-kāliʾ.”
It was narrated by al-Dāraquṭnī (3/71), al-Ḥākim (2/57), al-Baghawī in Sharḥ al-Sunnah (8/113), and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (1280).
In al-Bazzār’s narration:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prohibited shighār, the sale of what is in the womb, gharar sales, the sale of deferred debt for deferred debt, and exchanging what is deferred for what is immediate.”
He explained: “What is in the womb refers to unborn offspring; gharar is to sell what you do not possess; deferred debt for deferred debt means one debt in exchange for another debt; and exchanging deferred for immediate is when a man owes you one thousand dirhams and says: ‘Take five hundred immediately and waive the remainder.’”
Al-Dāraquṭnī said: “The linguists said that it means deferred payment for deferred payment.”
Al-Ḥākim said: “This hadith is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim.”
The correct judgment is that it is weak.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: “There is no authentic hadith concerning this, but the people are unanimously agreed that selling one debt for another debt is impermissible.”
Al-Shāfiʿī said: “The hadith scholars consider this hadith weak.”
Abū ʿUbayd said: “Al-kāliʾ for al-kāliʾ means deferred payment for deferred payment.”
The jurists have given many examples of this form of deferred-for-deferred sale.
